children: was in the spotlight on Thursday as Wall Street weighed in on the company's Oktane conference, with some praising the company amid increased momentum.

Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci raised his price target on Okta to $227 from $188 and said he's “optimistic” after what he heard at the event, especially as it increases its focus on artificial intelligence.

“Reflecting on what we heard at Oktane, we remain optimistic on the opportunity ahead for Okta as the company backs up its marketing around AI with product that seems to be gaining momentum, though it is still very early days,” DiFucci wrote in a note to clients. “Away from the AI buzz, we still continue to believe in Okta's more immediate opportunity that we highlighted more than two years ago ... with Okta Identity Governance
and Okta Privileged Access (OPA) down market.”
DiFucci reiterated his Buy rating on Okta.
Stifel analyst Adam Borg also reiterated his Buy rating and upped his price target to $215 from $180 and said the company is making further inroads with customers.

“Regarding AI, customers were generally early in their production AI journey (and associated AI identity security journey), but were interested in learning more about Okta's new O4AA innovation,” Borg wrote in a note to clients. “Net/net, we are pleased to see Okta's continued breadth of product innovation and our positive conference checks, and continue to believe that Identity remains a top security priority and that Okta has an emerging opportunity to secure AI. Collectively, we continue to believe the risk/reward remains skewed to the upside as Okta demonstrates traction securing non-human identities and looks to re-accelerate cRPO and revenue growth, and that shares can see multiple expansion as this plays out.”

title: Okta praised by Wall Street as annual conference focuses on AI
